answer.because: With unknown-options-as-args and halt-at-non-option both on and foo declared as a boolean, head parses ['./file.js', '--foo'] into {_: ['./file.js'], foo: true}, while base stops at the positional and gives {_: ['./file.js', '--foo']}; so removing the /^-/ guard sends the plain positional through pushPositional and parsing never halts (the finding's exact input, with foo undeclared, gives the same output on both trees because '--foo' is then unknown too).

why: With unknown-options-as-args and halt-at-non-option both on and foo declared as a boolean, head parses ['./file.js', '--foo'] into {_: ['./file.js'], foo: true}, while base stops at the positional and gives {_: ['./file.js', '--foo']}; so removing the /^-/ guard sends the plain positional through pushPositional and parsing never halts (the finding's exact input, with foo undeclared, gives the same output on both trees because '--foo' is then unknown too).
